EcoSort helps you learn how to separate waste according to Malaysian recycling standards. Proper waste separation reduces landfill pollution and protects our environment.
Food scraps, banana peels, vegetable waste, dry leaves.
These items decompose naturally. In Malaysia, they can be composted to create fertilizer for gardens.
Plastic bottles, aluminum cans, paper, cardboard, glass jars.
Ensure they are clean and dry. Place them in recycling bins or bring them to a recycling centre.
Batteries, light bulbs, e-waste (old phones, cables), chemicals.
These contain toxic materials. NEVER put in normal bins. Find e-waste collection points at malls or SWCorp centres.

string-array.name: eco_tips
string-array.item: 💡 Batteries contain lead and mercury — always send them to hazardous bins.
💡 Banana peels decompose naturally — they\'re organic waste.
💡 Plastic bottles can be recycled into new fabric!
💡 Malaysia\'s SWCorp provides scheduled e-waste collection — check their site.
💡 Egg shells are great organic compost material.
💡 Cardboard must be dry to be properly recycled.
💡 CFL bulbs contain mercury — treat them as hazardous waste.
